records.title: Bicocca International Scholarship Programme (BISP) — Università degli Studi di Milano-Bicocca
records.deadline_display: No separate application is required: all applicants to eligible programmes are automatically considered for the scholarship.

source.raw_extract:
The scholarship is awarded to the top student for each **Bachelor's** and **Master's degree programme taught in English**, including single-cycle degree programmes. No separate application is required: all applicants to eligible programmes are automatically considered for the scholarship.

The scholarship amounts to **€10,000 per year (gross)**, plus an exemption from tuition fees.

For more information, visit the official page **[here](https://en.unimib.it/study/information-international-students/bicocca-international-scholarship)**.
source.notes: Confidence HIGH applies to the UNKNOWN determination, i.e. high confidence that no scholarship deadline could be established. The only official portal page I could fetch for BISP publishes no deadline at all — it says the award is automatic and then defers to the en.unimib.it scholarship page, which is the page that would carry any deadline. That page is unreachable from this client: https://en.unimib.it/study/information-international-students/bicocca-international-scholarship returns HTTP 403. BISP deadlines track each individual degree programme's own admission call, and brief section 5 forbids substituting a generic admissions deadline for a different programme, so no date was written. Search-engine snippets for this page were deliberately NOT used as evidence (brief section 5).

records.title: RMIT Future Leaders Scholarship

source.as_of: eligibility stated for "offer letter to commence from 2026 intakes onwards"; page footer "Copyright © 2026 RMIT University"
source.raw_extract:
### No scholarship application is required

### Apply to study at RMIT

Follow our step-by-step guide on how to apply to RMIT as an international student.

If you are successful, you will receive an offer letter with the scholarship details outlined.

[from Eligibility]  have an offer letter to commence from 2026 intakes onwards in one of the following programs at RMIT:  
    -   Bachelor degree
    -   Masters by Coursework
source.notes: Transparency on the label: RMIT never uses the words "rolling" or "no deadline" anywhere on this page, so ROLLING is not a verbatim classification. It rests on three things read on the provider's own scholarship page: (1) the verbatim "No scholarship application is required"; (2) the award is applied automatically to tuition fees via the offer letter rather than an application with a window; (3) eligibility is open-ended - "have an offer letter to commence from 2026 intakes onwards" - with no closing date published. I also fetched the International Scholarships Terms and Conditions page RMIT links from the Future Leaders terms, and it contains no application-deadline statement either (its only date language is "if the scholarship is not accepted within the specified date on the scholarship letter", which concerns accepting an offer, not applying). No calendar date is written, per brief section 6. A reviewer who requires the explicit word "rolling" should downgrade this to UNKNOWN.

records.notes: No date written. RMIT publishes no closing date and there is no scholarship application step to close.

source.notes: FCT states an explicit calendar deadline of 2026-03-31 (17:00 Lisbon). That date is in the past as of retrieval on 2026-10-05, while the record is verification_status=active (open/upcoming), so per brief section 6 this is expired_mismatch: the stale date is deliberately NOT written and was NOT silently moved to 2027. FCT's own Expected Calls tab was fetched and shows "There are currently no Calls.", so no 2027 dates are published anywhere as of 2026-10-05. deadline_semantics is recorded as EXACT because that is genuinely the source's precision; deadline_date is null solely because the value is expired. FCT's remark that the call "takes place each year in March" is recurring-timer context only and is not used to derive any date.

records.title: Danish Government Scholarship
records.deadline_display: The scholarships are administered by the Danish universities, who each select the students, who are awarded with a scholarship.

source.publisher: Study in Denmark (studyindenmark.dk), managed by the Danish Ministry of Science, Higher Education and Digital Affairs
source.as_of: no cycle or date stated on the page
source.raw_extract:
Danish universities receive a limited number of government scholarships each year to fund highly qualified full-degree students from non-EU/EEA countries and Switzerland.

The scholarships are administered by the Danish universities, who each select the students, who are awarded with a scholarship.

For further information about the government scholarship, please consult the admission details of the higher education institution of your choice.
source.notes: Confidence HIGH applies to the UNKNOWN determination. Two independent reasons no deadline could be written. First, the record's own official_source_url, studies.ku.dk/education/student-life/finances-and-scholarships/scholarships-for-international-students, returns HTTP 404 - it is dead. Second, and more fundamentally, a university admissions page is not an official source for a Danish government award under brief section 4, so the hierarchy required going to the government domain. The national government page publishes no application deadline and explicitly hands the timing to each individual institution: "The scholarships are administered by the Danish universities, who each select the students" and "please consult the admission details of the higher education institution of your choice." I could therefore find no single official date, and per brief section 5 another university's deadline, or the national Optagelse.dk admissions deadline, may not be borrowed. Semantics recorded as UNKNOWN rather than ANNUAL because although the page says awards are made "each year", it states no annual timing window and no date - a "recurring" precision would imply a national annual schedule that does not exist.

records.notes: No national deadline exists to record. Timing is institution-specific by design. A per-institution deadline could only be recovered by a record whose official_source is that specific university.

records.title: Rufford Small Grants Programme
records.deadline_display: There are no deadlines – you can apply at any time of year.

source.as_of: page footer "© 2026 The Rufford Foundation"; no cycle stated
source.raw_extract: There are no deadlines – you can apply at any time of year. You can only make one funding application in any 12-month period. If your application is rejected, you must wait 12 months before you can reapply. If you are funded, you cannot apply for further support for at least 12 months.
source.exact_deadline_wording: There are no deadlines – you can apply at any time of year.
source.notes: The cleanest ROLLING in the shard: the provider states in its own words that there are no deadlines and that applications can be made at any time of year. Confirmed independently on a second official Foundation page, the FAQ, which answers the question "What are the deadlines?" with "There are no deadlines, you can apply at any time of year." No calendar date is written, per brief section 6. The record's cached deadline_precision of "varies" is not what the source says; rolling is. The one-app-per-12-months rule is a per-applicant eligibility limit, not a deadline, and is deliberately not converted into a date.
